subject.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget

question: Should the approved recovery-fuse implementation be reconstructed onto re-rooted current main as the canonical fix?
rationale: The implementation direction is approved and proof-positive, but the current branch cannot land normally; a large semantics-sensitive transplant requires explicit maintainer ownership and exact-head revalidation.

options.title: Reconstruct approved patch
options.body: Port the final reviewed logical diff onto current main, preserve the centralized state/store invariants, and repeat all proof.

options.title: Adopt another candidate
options.body: Use another PR only after it reaches equivalent architecture, maintainer approval, race coverage, upgrade evidence, and real behavior proof.

options.title: Pause the canonical fix
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open while maintainers revisit the recovery contract or reduce the landing scope.

recommendation.title: Reconstruct approved patch
recommendation.body: Port the final reviewed logical diff onto current main, preserve the centralized state/store invariants, and repeat all proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned approving reviewer and author of the final architecture, making them the safest owner for a semantics-preserving reconstruction.
